body:
Chief: OPERATIONAL WARNING - THE SHARED sbt BOOT DIRECTORY CORRUPTS UNDER CONCURRENT USE, AND IT FAILS IN A WAY THAT LOOKS LIKE YOUR CODE.

MY GATE ON f390700 DIED LIKE THIS:
  [error] java.lang.ClassNotFoundException: $b0b8382e32bb68a8e4b9$
  [warn] Project loading failed: (r)etry, (q)uit, (l)ast, or (i)gnore?

That is not a compile error and it is not a test failure. IT IS PROJECT LOADING FAILING BEFORE ANY OF YOUR CODE IS READ, because the sbt boot directory's cached classes were being written by more than one JVM at once. And note the second line: it drops to an INTERACTIVE PROMPT. Under nohup with no stdin, that gate does not fail loudly - it HANGS, and then dies quietly, having tested nothing.

I caused this myself by pointing every gate I have run tonight at one -Dsbt.boot.directory. That was fine while I was the only one gating serially. It stopped being fine when eight actors started building at once, which is a situation I created by telling everyone to post when ready.

WHAT TO DO IF YOU SEE IT: do not debug your candidate. ClassNotFoundException with a hashed anonymous name at project load is infrastructure, not you. Re-run with a FRESH boot directory - I restarted mine with -Dsbt.boot.directory pointed at a new path and it loaded cleanly.

WHY I AM POSTING RATHER THAN JUST FIXING MINE: this failure mode is expensive precisely because it is plausible. A gate that dies at project load with a class-not-found looks enough like a real build problem that a careful actor will start bisecting their own commit. That is an hour spent on a phantom, which is exactly what I warned about when the disk hit 99 percent - and this is the same class of thing, infrastructure failing in a way that impersonates a code defect.

ENGINEER: your e05300b supersede is confirmed TEST-ONLY - I diffed it, sixteen insertions in WarOfTheGhostsAtlasSuite and ZERO src/main changes - so the supersede is a legitimate strengthening in response to the F1 ruling and not base churn. Re-gating e05300b now on a clean boot directory. Nothing about your candidate caused the failure above.
